blocks.body: # Esperto feedback text and score thresholds

## The feedback capture is complete; one threshold correction is required

All **61 scored questions** now have feedback captured at **five Esperto source levels**, yielding **305 non-empty records**. The implementation-ready mapping is **0–2, 3–4, 5–6, 7–8, and 9–10**. A live 0-through-10 sweep of question 1 proves the top feedback starts at score 9, so the platform's provisional **7–9 / 10-only** split does not match current Esperto behavior for that question.

## Five stored levels explain four visible answers on question 1

Question 1 displays the same text from 0 through 4 because its level-0 and level-3 source texts are identical. That visible collapse must not be mistaken for a four-level system: two other questions contain different text at levels 0 and 3. Preserve all five stored records.

## The source library covers every question at every sampled level

Five official uniform-fill reports expose one feedback response per question at scores 0, 3, 5, 7, and 10. The catalogue joins these records by exact question label and overlays current live wording for question 1, where the August report differs from the May sample.

## What the score map means

A **source level** is one of the five answers used to expose Esperto's stored feedback text: 0, 3, 5, 7, or 10. A **score range** is the set of integer answers that should select that stored text. A **visible range** can span more than one stored level when adjacent levels contain identical wording.

## Duplicate wording hides some transitions

Most questions use identical text at levels 0 and 3, so a report-only experiment cannot see that low boundary unless it varies one of the two questions whose texts differ. The source catalogue therefore retains duplicate records and records provenance instead of deduplicating them.

## The evidence combines uniform source reports with a live boundary sweep

The five May reports established the text selected at each source stop for all 61 questions. Eleven live August reports then varied only Effective recruitment process from 0 through 10 while holding the other answers constant. Comparing the selected text located live transitions at 5, 7, and 9 and exposed current wording drift.

## One boundary remains inferred rather than question-by-question proven

The mapping **0–2 / 3–4 / 5–6 / 7–8 / 9–10** is the best-supported common five-band model. Scores 1, 2, and 4 have not been swept on a question whose level-0 and level-3 texts differ, so the low interior boundary is a high-confidence inference, not direct vendor confirmation. The other 60 questions also retain May wording unless independently refreshed.

## Implement five bands and preserve provenance

Use five stored feedback records with score ranges **0–2, 3–4, 5–6, 7–8, and 9–10**. Keep duplicate texts as separate records. Treat question 1 as current-live wording and the remaining catalogue as May 2026 source wording. Do not describe every interior boundary as vendor-confirmed.

## Smallest remaining parity check

If exact vendor parity is required, sweep scores 0 through 4 on **Financial alert function** or **Employees know yearly goal**. Those are the only two questions whose level-0 and level-3 texts differ, so either one can reveal the hidden low-end transition with five reports.
